ext_description.message: Blocks ads and trackers quietly. No paid exceptions for advertisers, no telemetry, no data collection.
ext_description.description: Store summary and manifest description, at most 132 characters.

menu_hide_element.description: Right-click menu entry on web pages (D-106). Quoted in perm_active_tab_why, perm_context_menus_why, onboarding_hide_text and the docs: change them together.

level_light_note.message: Blocks network requests only. Use when a page misbehaves.

level_standard_note.message: Also hides leftover ad boxes and stops ad scripts.

level_thorough_note.message: Also scans each page for generic ad boxes. Slightly slower.

onboarding_unavailable.message: Could not read the current settings. Protection is on with safe defaults; you can close this tab.

onboarding_protected_text.message: Ads, trackers and known malware sites are blocked from now on.

onboarding_access_on.message: Site access: allowed on all sites

onboarding_access_why.message: We need it to hide leftover ad boxes and stop ad scripts.

onboarding_access_never.message: We never read, store or send what you browse.

onboarding_access_off.message: Site access is off, so only Light mode works: requests are blocked, but leftover ad boxes stay and ad scripts run.

onboarding_extras_text.message: Optional. All off until you turn them on; change them any time in the dashboard.

onboarding_extra_cookies_note.message: Hides the banners; you do not accept or refuse anything.

onboarding_extra_annoyances_note.message: Overlays, social buttons, chat widgets and notification prompts.

onboarding_extra_language_note.message: Suggested from your browser language. Blocks ads made for sites in that language.

onboarding_pin_text.message: Open the puzzle-piece menu next to the address bar and choose the pin next to the name, so the icon stays in view.

onboarding_hide_text.message: Right-click what you want gone and choose "Hide this…", or open the toolbar panel and choose "Hide something".

onboarding_break_text.message: Open the toolbar panel and choose "Something wrong with this page?". It walks you through the fix.

onboarding_some_refused.message: Some choices could not be turned on. See the message next to them.

onboarding_access_denied.message: Site access was not allowed. Light mode stays on.

onboarding_done_text.message: You can close this tab. Settings are in the dashboard whenever you need them.

pack_note_trackers.message: Blocks trackers that follow you between sites.

pack_note_malware.message: Blocks sites known for malware and scams.

pack_note_popups.message: Blocks sites known for pop-up ads, as whole pages.

pack_note_cookies.message: Hides cookie banners. Works best with Thorough.

pack_note_annoy_overlays.message: Hides boxes that cover the page, such as newsletter sign-ups.

pack_note_annoy_social.message: Hides share and like buttons of social networks.

pack_note_annoy_widgets.message: Hides chat bubbles and assistant widgets.

pack_note_annoy_newsletters.message: Hides other distractions listed by EasyList Annoyances.

pack_note_annoy_notifications.message: Hides prompts that ask to send you notifications.

pack_note_params.message: Removes tracking codes from addresses. A rare page may need them.

pack_note_gpc.message: Tells sites you do not want your data sold or shared.

hidden_empty.message: Open the toolbar panel on a page and choose "Hide something".

hidden_unreadable.message: Your hidden items could not be read. Nothing was changed.

hidden_removed.message: Removed. It shows again on that site. If a page still hides it, reload that page.

dprivacy_gpc_note.message: Tells every site you visit that you do not want your data sold or shared. It stays on in Light mode.

dprivacy_badge.message: Show the number of blocked requests on the toolbar icon

dprivacy_badge_note.message: Chrome counts them for the current tab. The number never leaves your browser.

dprivacy_needs_access.message: Needs site access to all sites; until then it has no effect.

dprivacy_requests.message: $PRODUCT$ makes no network requests. New rules arrive only through Chrome's own extension updates. There is no telemetry, no analytics and no crash reporting. The one exception is yours to make: "Open a new issue" in a problem report opens github.com in a browser tab with the report you reviewed.

dprivacy_stored_heading.message: What is stored on this device

dprivacy_stored_settings.message: Your settings: default level, packs, and the level, pause and pop-up choice of each site you set (site names only, never page addresses).

dprivacy_stored_hidden.message: Elements you chose to hide, with the name of their site.

dprivacy_stored_rules.message: The packaged filter rules, which are public.

dprivacy_not_stored.message: No browsing history is kept. What the toolbar panel shows about a page is read when you open it and forgotten within a minute.

dprivacy_not_requested_heading.message: Permissions we do not ask for

dprivacy_pledge_1.message: No paid allowlisting, no "acceptable ads", no affiliate links, no ads of our own.

dprivacy_pledge_2.message: No telemetry. No analytics. No remote configuration.

dprivacy_pledge_3.message: No network request unless you turn on a feature that needs one; each such feature is listed here with the exact host it contacts.

dprivacy_pledge_4.message: Minimal permissions, each explained on this page; new ones only for a shipped feature.

dprivacy_pledge_5.message: Every store release can be rebuilt from its public source, and the hashes are published.

dprivacy_pledge_6.message: The listing will not be sold or transferred without 90 days of public notice.

dprivacy_pledge_7.message: Publishing needs verified uploads and two-step verification; who can publish is public.

dprivacy_pledge_8.message: Changes to this pledge are versioned and announced in the changelog.

dprivacy_verify.message: Release builds are reproducible: rebuilding the published source tag gives the same files. The repository document "Verify a build" has the commands and the hashes to compare.

perm_dnr_why.message: Chrome blocks ads, trackers and malware sites itself, from the rules in this package. We never see the requests.

perm_all_urls_name.message: Read and change all your data on all websites

perm_all_urls_why.message: Needed to hide leftover ad boxes, stop ad scripts and show the pop-up blocked page. Nothing is read, stored or sent: the work happens inside each page. Light mode works without it.

perm_scripting_why.message: Lets Chrome insert our packaged hiding and anti-ad scripts into pages, even while the extension sleeps.

perm_storage_why.message: Keeps short-lived state for this browser session and the elements you chose to hide.

perm_unlimited_storage_why.message: Stops Chrome from deleting your settings when the disk is nearly full.

perm_active_tab_name.message: Access the current tab when you click the icon

perm_active_tab_why.message: After you click the icon (or choose "Hide this…"), lets the extension work in that one tab: show what was blocked there, start the element hider and briefly show something you hid.

perm_context_menus_why.message: Adds "Hide this…" to the right-click menu of pages, for the element hider.

perm_alarms_why.message: Turns protection back on when a pause ends.

perm_tabs_why.message: We never list your tabs or the pages you visit.

perm_web_navigation_why.message: We never follow where you go.

perm_web_request_why.message: We never watch your network traffic.

perm_dnr_feedback_why.message: We never read the addresses that were blocked; counts come from Chrome.
